hypotheses.title: Curcumin Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Oral curcumin supplementation extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving curcumin will show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Curcumin modulates inflammatory signaling and oxidative stress responses, both of which drive age-related tissue decline. Suppressing these processes should slow the accumulation of damage that limits lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Curcumin-treated mice will exhibit significantly longer median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to curcumin-supplemented or control diets, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: Melatonin Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Melatonin supplementation extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving exogenous melatonin will show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Melatonin is a potent antioxidant and circadian regulator, and circadian disruption accelerates aging across tissues. Restoring robust melatonin signaling should reduce oxidative damage and improve systemic homeostasis.
hypotheses.prediction: Melatonin-treated mice will exhibit significantly longer median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to melatonin-supplemented or control diets, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: Melatonin Extends Lifespan by Restoring Pineal Function
hypotheses.claim: Melatonin extends lifespan in Mus musculus by restoring pineal melatonin production. Mice receiving exogenous melatonin will show increased median and maximal lifespan through reactivation of endogenous pineal output.
hypotheses.rationale: Pineal melatonin production declines with age, weakening circadian coordination and antioxidant defenses. Exogenous melatonin that re-establishes pineal signaling should restore these protective functions and extend lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Melatonin-treated mice will live significantly longer than controls, and the effect will correlate with restored markers of pineal melatonin synthesis.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat one group of aging mice with melatonin and another with vehicle, then compare survival while measuring pineal melatonin-synthesis gene expression; include a pinealectomized arm to test dependence on the gland.

hypotheses.title: N-acetyl-L-cysteine Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: N-acetyl-L-cysteine supplementation extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving N-acetyl-L-cysteine will show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: N-acetyl-L-cysteine replenishes glutathione, the principal cellular antioxidant, thereby buffering reactive oxygen species that accumulate with age. Sustained antioxidant capacity should slow molecular damage and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: N-acetyl-L-cysteine-treated mice will exhibit significantly longer median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to N-acetyl-L-cysteine-supplemented or control diets, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: TM5441 Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: TM5441, a plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 inhibitor, extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving TM5441 will show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: PAI-1 rises with age and promotes fibrosis, vascular stiffening, and cellular senescence. Pharmacological inhibition of PAI-1 should preserve tissue function and thereby extend lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: TM5441-treated mice will exhibit significantly longer median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to TM5441 or vehicle administration, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: Caffeic Acid Phenethyl Ester Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Caffeic acid phenethyl ester supplementation extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving caffeic acid phenethyl ester will show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Caffeic acid phenethyl ester suppresses chronic inflammatory signaling and oxidative stress, processes that accelerate tissue degeneration. Dampening these pathways should preserve organ function and extend lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Caffeic acid phenethyl ester-treated mice will exhibit significantly longer median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to caffeic acid phenethyl ester-supplemented or control diets, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: Melatonin Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Melatonin supplementation shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving exogenous melatonin will show a measurable decrease in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Chronic exogenous melatonin can desynchronize endogenous circadian rhythms and blunt receptor sensitivity, disrupting hormonal cycles that coordinate metabolism and repair. Sustained circadian disruption should accelerate age-related decline.
hypotheses.prediction: Melatonin-treated mice will exhibit significantly shorter median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to melatonin-supplemented or control diets, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: N-acetyl-L-cysteine Extends Lifespan via Insulin/IGF-1 Signaling
hypotheses.claim: N-acetyl-L-cysteine extends lifespan in Mus musculus by activating the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway. Mice receiving N-acetyl-L-cysteine will show increased median and maximal lifespan through enhanced insulin/IGF-1 signaling activity.
hypotheses.rationale: Insulin/IGF-1 signaling promotes growth, tissue maintenance, and stress resistance when appropriately activated. N-acetyl-L-cysteine-induced redox changes can modulate this pathway, and its activation should support repair processes that extend lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: N-acetyl-L-cysteine-treated mice will live significantly longer than controls, and the extension will correlate with elevated insulin/IGF-1 pathway activity.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat mice with N-acetyl-L-cysteine or vehicle, compare survival, and measure insulin/IGF-1 pathway activation; include a group with pathway-specific inhibition to test whether the lifespan effect is abolished.

hypotheses.title: C60 Fullerene Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: C60 fullerene supplementation extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving C60 fullerene will show a measurable increase in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: C60 fullerene is a highly efficient radical scavenger that can localize in lipid membranes and mitochondria. Long-lasting neutralization of oxidative damage in these compartments should slow aging and extend lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: C60 fullerene-treated mice will exhibit significantly longer median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to C60 fullerene or vehicle administration, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.

hypotheses.title: N-acetyl-L-cysteine Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: N-acetyl-L-cysteine supplementation shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Mice receiving N-acetyl-L-cysteine will show a measurable decrease in median and maximal lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Reactive oxygen species serve as signaling molecules required for adaptive stress responses and cellular repair. Excessive antioxidant buffering by N-acetyl-L-cysteine can suppress these signals, weakening hormesis and accelerating age-related decline.
hypotheses.prediction: N-acetyl-L-cysteine-treated mice will exhibit significantly shorter median and maximum lifespans than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of genetically uniform mice to N-acetyl-L-cysteine-supplemented or control diets, house both groups identically, and follow them until natural death with blinded survival analysis.
